Git found no common ancestor between the two histories you’re trying to merge. In other words, it sees them as separate projects—often because one repository was initialized independently, or the remote points to a different repository or branch.

Check that you have the right remote and branch. If the histories really are meant to be combined, you can explicitly allow it:

```bash
git merge <branch> --allow-unrelated-histories
```

Resolve any conflicts Git reports, then commit the merge. Don’t use that option until you’ve confirmed the histories should be joined.
